queries.evidence_ja: 一日々々いろ〳〵なことに疲らされなやまされ苦しまされても
queries.reason: The concessive ても is dropped. The Japanese is “even though [we are] tired out, troubled and made to suffer day by day by all sorts of things”, but the English becomes a bare participial list followed by the two-years clause, losing the husband's concession—he is conceding the suffering, not merely listing it.
queries.say: The concessive in the husband's count of the years is missing.
queries.span: Tired and troubled and made to suffer day by day by one thing and another
queries.suggested_fix: Even if we are worn out and troubled and made to suffer day by day by one thing and another

queries.evidence_ja: 二年はもう過ぎたんだからな
queries.reason: 二年は with the emphatic は means “two years at least have already passed”. Without “at least”, the English flatly contradicts the three-years count the house reading requires be kept exact and repeated (p14, p22, p25, p27): the reader is told the marriage is three years old and then that two years are past.
queries.say: “Two years are already past” reads as an exact figure against the three years elsewhere.
queries.suggested_fix: two years at least are already past

queries.reason: あとを片づける is tidying up after the meal, not clearing away “what is left”, which in English suggests leftover food. The distinction matters to the crux: the close must stay deliberately practical housework, not a remark about the meal's remains.
queries.say: “Clear up what is left” points at leftovers rather than tidying up after supper.
queries.span: let us clear up what is left

data.say: Two queries on p28, where the husband's concession and his “two years at least” are flattened against the three-years measure, and one small practical mistranslation at p36; the storm frame and the closing quiet come through plain and linked, and the rest of the page is clean.
